name: Pale-Titan
description: Pale-Titan fills the sky like a slow-turning pearl, banded in bone-white and faint rose ammonia cloud. Its single great storm—the Pale Eye—has drifted the equator twice per local year, a vortex wide enough to swallow four terrestrial worlds. Around it spins a ring of shattered ice and moon-fragments, bright enough to read by when seen from the inner moons.

Nothing lands here; nothing can. Probes that descend past the cloud decks stop transmitting at a suspiciously consistent depth, their last frames showing structures in the cloud layers too regular to be wind-shear. The magnetic poles wander in slow circles rather than sitting still, dragging auroral storms across entire hemispheres like searchlights.

In orbit above the north pole drifts the Satellite Graveyard: two hundred derelict probes from nine different civilizations, each from a culture that never contacted another, each destroyed by micrometeorite within months of arrival. And among them turns a functioning beacon, transmitting a repeating sequence on no known protocol—older than every wreck around it, and still drawing power from somewhere.

Helium-3 skimmers work the outer bands under heavy insurance, because one in nine never comes back up. The moons' mining guilds have quietly stopped asking what happened to them. Whoever decodes the beacon's sequence will either own the richest fuel claim in the sector or learn why two hundred civilizations' eyes went dark in the same spot.
